      <link>https://www.nrk.no/nyheter/kongen-fullforte-maraton-pa-tiden-4.43.01-1.18076803</link>
      <description>Kongen og kronprinsessen er deltakere i French Riviera Marathon, i Nice sør i Frankrike.
Kong Haakon løp i mål på tiden 4.43.01, ifølge sporingstjenesten Trackanza.
Det var TV 2 som meldte saken først.
Et bilde viser kongen og kronprinsessen løpende ved siden av hverandre under maratonet. I maratonet er kronprinsessen registrert som Ingrid Alexandra og kongen som Haakon Magnus.
Startskuddet gikk klokka 09.16, og distansen er helmaraton på 42,125 kilometer. Løypen går langs den franske rivieraen fra Nice til Cannes.
Lørdag formiddag opplyste Slottet på nettsidene sine at «statsrådet forestår bestyrelsen av riket».
Ifølge nettsidene var kongen og kronprinsessen på privat opphold i utlandet. Det betyr at regjeringen har ansvaret for å styre og forvalte landet.
(NTB/NRK)</description>

      <title>Ny norsk gulltriumf i VM i skyting</title>
      <link>https://www.nrk.no/sport/ny-norsk-gulltriumf-i-vm-i-skyting-1.18076796</link>
      <description>Caroline Finnestad Lund, Jeanette Hegg Duestad og Synnøve Berg tok laggullet på 50 meter rifle match i VM i skyting i Doha søndag.
Det var Lunds andre gull i mesterskapet. Lørdag ble 21-åringen verdensmester på 50 meter 60 skudd liggende.
Norge sanket totalt 1764 poeng under lagkonkurransen, og de kom 3,0 poeng foran Sveits på 2.-plass. Tsjekkia stakk av med bronsemedaljen. De var to poeng bak sveitserne igjen.
I eliminasjonen for lag 1 ble Finnestad Lund nummer fire med 588 poeng. Synnøve Berg ble nummer sju med 586 poeng. Duestad ble nummer tre med 590 poeng i lag 2.
Alle de tre norske jentene er videre til kvalifiseringen i den individuelle konkurransen i den samme øvelsen mandag. (NTB)</description>

      <link>https://www.nrk.no/nyheter/flere-skadet-etter-kraftig-jordskjelv-sentralt-i-japan-1.18076688</link>
      <description>Minst 22 personer ble skadet da et jordskjelv med styrke 5,5 rammet Shizuoka-prefekturet i det sentrale Japan. Butikkvinduer ble knust, og folk rømte ut av bygninger.
Ifølge kringkasteren NHK er det ikke fare for tsunamier.
Skjelvet inntraff rundt klokka 1 natt til søndag. Det hadde en dybde på 41 kilometer. Den foreløpige målingen fra Japans meteorologiske institutt, som har ansvaret for overvåking og varsling av jordskjelv, var på 5,7.
Det amerikanske jordskjelvsenteret USGS målte det til 5,5.
I naboprefekturet Aichi ble det målt kraftige rystelser på nivå 5+ på den japanske skalaen – det sterkeste som er registrert der siden 1997.

      <description>Israels president har gitt opposisjonsleder Gadi Eisenkot i oppdrag å prøve danne regjering.
Hverken partiene som støtter statsminister Benjamin Netanyahu eller partiene som støtter Eisenkot fikk flertall ved valget 27. november.
Netanyahus blokk fikk 53 plasser i Knesset, mens blokken til Eisenkot fikk 48 mandater.
For å få flertall og bli statsminister trenger man 61 plasser i nasjonalforsamlingen. Begge blokkene er avhengig av de 19 mandatene fra de palestinsk-arabiske partiene, mend både Netanyahu og Eisenkot har sagt de ikke vil forhandle med dem.</description>

      <description>Politiet opplyser at det har vært en front-mot-front-ulykke på E6 like ved Eidsvoll-tunnelen i sørgående løp.

      <description>Thomas Markle ble pågrepet av føderale agenter i nærheten av Tampa i Florida fredag morgen amerikansk tid.

    <item>
      <title>NFF innfører semiautomatisert offside i Eliteserien</title>
      <link>https://www.nrk.no/sport/nff-innforer-semiautomatisert-offside-i-eliteserien-1.18075445</link>
      <description>Det opplyser Fotballforbundet på en pressekonferanse fredag.
– Prisen har kommet ned til et nivå som gjør at muligheten er der, sier generalsekretær Karl-Petter Løken.
Han opplyser at innføringen vil skje i tråd med et dommerløft. NFF bevilger 5,5 millioner kroner i 2027 til dommerløftet, og 3,5 millioner av dem skal få til semiautomatisert offside.
NFF ønsker å øke dette til 7,5 millioner kroner i 2028, og gradvis trappe opp mot 2030.
– Det du har sett med disse linjene blir borte og du får disse visningene med menneskekropper hvor du ser helt tydelig at det er offside. Det er semiautomatisert offside. Det er det ene løftet, sier Løken og fortsetter:
– Det er en utgift som tas én gang og som vil følge oss, og så vil vi trappe opp resten av investeringen i dommerutviklingene i de andre tiltakene i tillegg. Så det blir en gradvis opptrapping, eksempelvis profesjonalisering. Vi starter stille og rolig og så blir det flere og flere.
Dette skjer etter et VAR-oppgjør blant flere toppklubber. Roenborg satt ned et eget utvalg som konkluderte med at «Dagens VAR fungerer for dårlig under norske forhold. De lovte forbedringene har ikke løst hovedutfordringene, og kostnadene er for høye i forhold til kvaliteten».
Utvalget til Rosenborg stilte seg også tvilende til at semiautomatisert offside ville hjelpe VAR i norsk fotball.
– Så det vil være penger ut av vinduet hvis tinget sier nei (til VAR)? spør NRK.
– Vi kommer ikke til å diskutere detaljer i den avtalen, svarer Klaveness.</description>

]]>

After BC Highway Patrol’s annual Drive Relative to Conditions campaign resulted in almost 1,200 fewer tickets this year than last year, the RCMP agency says that may not indicate that drivers are getting the message.

In 2025 across the province, BC Highway Patrol officers handed out 7,888 tickets, of which 1,598 were on Vancouver Island.

This year, a total of 6,695 tickets were written across the province, with 1,315 on Vancouver Island.

This means the total number of tickets dropped by 1,193 across the province and 283 on Vancouver Island.

“A drop in staffing levels appears to be one of the reasons for this year’s lower enforcement numbers,” BC Highway Patrol said in a news release.

A driver in Merritt was cited as an example that dangerous driving in poor conditions is still a problem.

On Oct. 25, a driver on Highway 97C was caught on a radar driving 166 kilometres per hour in a 110 zone. The truck was also found to have not been inspected for mechanical modifications and defects after an earlier notice in August.

The 28-year-old driver from Abbotsford was given a seven day impound for excessive speeding, a ticket for excessive speed worth $368, a ticket for fail to comply with order, and a notice and order requiring the truck immediately have its insurance suspended until the mechanical defects are fixed and inspected.

“We ask all drivers to understand that posted speed limits are created for ideal, dry, clear, daytime conditions,” says Supt. Lori Orstad with BC Highway Patrol.

“Safe driving always starts with staying sober and alert, but you also need to slow down for poor weather, darkness, or heavy traffic – exactly the sort of conditions we see more in fall and winter.”

ICBC says that speeding is the leading contributing factor to fatal crashes in the province.

“Each year in B.C., speed is a factor in more than 2,400 crashes and leads to an average of 91 deaths,” the insurance agency says.

“So slow down and give yourself extra time to get to your destination. It’s not worth the risk to yourself or to others.”

]]> 1360336 Federal budget rink funding raises hopes for Vancouver Island hockey associations facing ice shortage https://cheknews.ca/federal-budget-rink-funding-raises-hopes-for-vancouver-island-hockey-associations-facing-ice-shortage-1360305/ Tue, 10 Nov 2026 17:45:00 +0000 https://cheknews.ca/?p=1360305

Hockey may be Canada's game, but on southern Vancouver Island, finding somewhere to play it is becoming increasingly difficult.

The post Federal budget rink funding raises hopes for Vancouver Island hockey associations facing ice shortage appeared first on CHEK.

]]>

Hockey may be Canada’s game, but on southern Vancouver Island, finding somewhere to play it is becoming increasingly difficult.

“We’re at capacity everywhere,” says Al McCullough, president of the Vancouver Island Amateur Hockey Association.

Whether you’re a hockey parent, player or administrator, the calls for more available ice are getting louder.

And the problem isn’t going away anytime soon.

Last week’s federal budget included a commitment of $750 million over nine years to build, expand and upgrade arenas across Canada. It’s money municipalities will soon be competing for, and Saanich’s new mayor is wasting little time getting in the game.

Mayor Rishi Sharma isn’t a hockey parent, but that didn’t stop him from getting to work early Saturday morning.

“I jumped on it. I drafted a letter to Minister [of Housing and Infrastructure and Minister responsible for Pacific Economic Development Canada Gregor] Robertson,” Sharma says.

The need is particularly acute on southern Vancouver Island. Of the approximately 9,000 minor hockey players on the Island, 60 per cent play south of the Malahat, sharing just 12 rinks. The remaining 40 per cent play north of the Malahat, where there are 24 rinks.

Watch the story below:

Loading the player...

Outside of Nanaimo, which is also stretched to capacity, much of the pressure is being felt on the South Island.

The Victoria Minor Hockey Association has even had to take an unprecedented step: turning children away.

“We’ve had to turn some kids away, and we historically have never done that,” says association president Katie Bernardo.

Making matters more challenging, the City of Victoria doesn’t have an ice rink of its own. The association relies on facilities in neighbouring Oak Bay, Esquimalt and Saanich to accommodate its players.

Bernardo says the association is in constant contact with neighbouring groups, including Peninsula and Juan de Fuca minor hockey, to find ways to make more ice available.

There is some relief on the horizon. Esquimalt’s Archie Browning Sports Centre is scheduled to reopen Dec. 5, providing some additional capacity.

However, the Ian Stewart Complex at the University of Victoria is scheduled to shut down in the spring, potentially adding more pressure to an already stretched system.

The situation is similarly tight on the West Shore.

“We have about 800 kids registered, and we have to stuff them all into three rinks,” says Juan de Fuca Minor Hockey Association president Sheryl Williamson.

And that’s before figure skaters get a single turn on the ice.

McCullough says addressing the shortage will require a coordinated effort from all levels of government.

“Our MLAs and our MPs and our city councils have to say, ‘Hey, what about us?'” he says.

Sharma says Saanich will be pushing to get its share of the federal funding, and he’s prepared to make some noise to ensure the community isn’t left out.

“You have to be that squeaky wheel, and Saanich now has me. I’m in their corner, but I don’t skate very well,” Sharma says.

With minor hockey associations already struggling to find enough ice time, the competition for new arenas and upgrades is about to heat up.

And this time, the biggest battle may be happening off the ice.

]]> 1360305 Popular Oak Bay playground set for decommissioning as replacement plans take shape https://cheknews.ca/popular-oak-bay-playground-set-for-decommissioning-as-replacement-plans-take-shape-1360325/ Tue, 10 Nov 2026 17:32:34 +0000 https://cheknews.ca/?p=1360325

]]>

An oceanfront playground in Oak Bay will be closing, with no timeline yet for when it will be replaced.

Willows Park is a popular summertime spot on the South Island, and the playground is now at the end of its useful life.

“Following recent technical assessments, the playground equipment at Willows Park will be decommissioned due to it being at the end of its useful life and inability to be maintained to meet safety standards,” the District of Oak Bay said on Facebook.

“We understand the enjoyment this playground has provided for the greater community. A report will be brought forward to Council in the new year regarding a project plan for the future of the park.”

The district says that staff will be developing a plan to identify new play features and other park improvements for Willows Park in the coming year.

The plan will include public engagement and outreach to the Songhees and Esquimalt First Nations, given the cultural significance of the area known as Sitchanalth to the Lekwungen.  

Following the announcement that the playground would be decommissioned, commenters shared memories of the play equipment.

“There was real joy swinging facing the beach, and feeling like we would fly over the water,” Amanda Weeks wrote. “It has been a delight to watch my own children enjoy this traditional piece of our collective past.”

“Hopefully a great new playground will be installed!” Brian Wagner wrote. “The kids have loved these. My kids loved them when they were little.”

Other commenters were critical of the announcement.

“This is devastating and not acceptable,” Mariah Welch wrote. “Parks should be proactively planned when we know the equipment is aging. Now our community suffers a loss, and I have to explain why we can’t go to a favourite park. I worry the process of getting approval for new equipment will take years.”

“When did you know it was reaching end of life?” Natalie Barnes asked. “Why wasn’t it replaced before it had to be decommissioned? This is our flagship gem of a park.”

]]> 1360324 Real estate association forecasts B.C. home sales to slide 4.5 per cent this year https://cheknews.ca/real-estate-association-forecasts-b-c-home-sales-to-slide-4-5-per-cent-this-year-1360319/ Tue, 10 Nov 2026 16:51:36 +0000 https://cheknews.ca/?p=1360319

The B.C. Real Estate Association expects home sales in the province to continue to slide this year, warning of "mounting headwinds" for the market, while hoping for a pick-up in both prices and sales in 2027.

The post Real estate association forecasts B.C. home sales to slide 4.5 per cent this year appeared first on CHEK.

]]>

The B.C. Real Estate Association expects home sales in the province to continue to slide this year, warning of “mounting headwinds” for the market, while hoping for a pick-up in both prices and sales in 2027.

The association says in its fourth-quarter forecast that sales are expected to fall 4.5 per cent this year from 2025 levels, to just over 67,000 units sold.

Association chief economist Brendon Ogmundson says in a statement that prospective buyers this year had several reasons to hesitate, including an oil-price shock, trade tensions with the United States, slower immigration and rising interest rates.

The forecast says active listings in B.C. are at their highest levels since 2015, and new-home inventory is also elevated.

It predicts that the supply pressure will push the average home price down 1.2 per cent to just over $941,000.

The forecast calls for a “modest recovery” in 2027 with sales projected to increase 7.2 per cent, but Ogmundson says that’s in anticipation of a decline in the impacts of new U.S. tariffs and reductions in fixed mortgage rates.

“Hopefully, a calming of these headwinds next year should stimulate housing activity, which, paired with flattening inventories, is expected to drive price growth of 2.4 per cent in 2027, bringing the provincial average price to $964,200,” the forecast says, adding it is anticipating a “long-awaited rebound” in the Lower Mainland market.

Greater Vancouver home sales are projected to reach 23,000 units this year, down 3 per cent from the year before, while the Fraser Valley is forecast to see a 4.4 per cent decrease to 11,000 units.

The largest decline is expected in the Chilliwack area of the Lower Mainland, with unit sales falling from 2,300 last year to 1,900 this year, an 18-per-cent decrease.

“Following a 2025 that saw the weakest year of sales in over a decade, faint signs of a 2026 recovery were thwarted by a resurgent oil price shock and further escalation in Canada’s trade war with the United States,” the forecast says.

“With population growth expected to remain subdued through 2027, B.C. faces limited capacity to grow at trend levels.”

Forestry industry leaders say Ottawa’s historic $6.5-billion funding package will give the sector a much-needed boost but won’t save struggling mills overnight.

The federal government’s spending plan announced last week proposes to roll out funding over six years to help modernize aging mills, boost productivity and develop new products.

But the money isn’t expected to start flowing until 2027-28, even as U.S. tariffs, weak markets and rising costs continue to threaten jobs and operations across the country.

Derek Nighbor, president and chief executive of the Forest Products Association of Canada, called the $6.5-billion commitment “precedent setting.”

But he warned that 2027 will likely be another difficult year for the industry as housing starts remain weak and U.S. tariffs persist.

The forestry sector has been battered by years of mill closures and layoffs.

Those struggles have intensified over the past several months, with pulp and paper mills across the country shutting down or suspending operations citing a range of market pressures.

In recent weeks, AV Group NB Inc. temporarily idled its pulp mill in Nackawic, N.B., affecting about 350 workers, while Rayonier Advanced Materials halted production at its Témiscaming, Que., facility, affecting more than 300 unionized jobs. 

Domtar also announced in August that it would indefinitely idle its Bayview Fibre chipping facility and Howe Sound pulp mill in Port Mellon, B.C., affecting about 400 employees. 

Ken Farr, president of the Canadian Institute of Forestry, said he worries the funding may come too late to help some struggling mills.

“The issue is now and the problem is now,” he said.

Farr said the industry is facing a “perfect storm” of U.S. tariffs, aging facilities and increasingly limited access to affordable timber supplies.

“I don’t think any kind of funding can be sent too soon,” he said. “It will help companies upgrade their equipment, raise productivity and transition to higher-value wood and paper products.”
